q.intro.text: Three bags hold the same number of marbles each. Together with six loose marbles, they balance twenty-seven marbles on the other pan. How many marbles are in one bag? Pick an answer, and say how sure you are.

e.intro.text: Four steps. Press each one. The balance moves first, then the notation.

e.step0.text: Start with x, the marbles in one bag. Times three gives the three bags. Plus six adds the loose marbles. That makes twenty-seven.

e.step1.text: The plus six was done last, so it comes off first. Take six off both pans: still level. Three x equals twenty-one.

e.step2.text: Now undo the times three. Split both pans into three equal shares: one bag balances seven marbles. x equals seven.

e.step3.text: Put the marbles back, and open the bags. Three times seven, plus six, is twenty-seven. Both pans match, so x equals seven is right.

e.why.text: Quick check. Why did the six come off before dividing by three?

e.why.ok.text: Yes. Undo a chain from the end, like taking off your shoes before your socks.

e.why.order.text: Try it. Twenty-seven divided by three is nine, then nine minus six is three. But three times three, plus six, is fifteen, not twenty-seven. Dividing first would have to split the six too.

e.why.move.text: Nothing moved across. Six came off both pans, and that is what kept them level.

t.intro.text: Now four bags and nine loose marbles balance thirty-three marbles. The first two steps are done for you.

t.move.text: What undoes the times four? Pick the move.

t.move.ok.text: Yes. Divide by four on both pans. Split each pan into four equal shares.

t.move.left.text: Watch. Only the left pan changed, so the balance tips. Whatever you do, do it to both sides.

t.move.times.text: Times four again would make sixteen bags. To undo a multiply, divide.

t.x.text: One bag balances how many marbles? x equals what?

t.x.times.text: Ninety-six is twenty-four times four. Undo a multiply with a divide: split twenty-four into four equal shares.

t.x.all.text: Twenty-four balances all four bags. One bag balances one share.

t.x.no.text: Count one share: twenty-four marbles split into four equal rows.

t.x.ok.text: Yes. Twenty-four divided by four is six. x equals six.

t.check.text: Check it. What is four times six, plus nine?

t.check.order.text: Multiply first. Four times six is twenty-four, then add nine.

t.check.no.text: Four times six is twenty-four, and twenty-four plus nine is what?

t.check.ok.text: Thirty-three, the same as the right pan. x equals six is right.

q.cb.right.text: At the start you picked seven, and you were right. Now you can show why: undo the last step first.

q.cb.order.text: At the start you picked three. That divides first, while the six is still on the pan. The six comes off first.

q.cb.fwd.text: At the start you picked eleven. That adds the six again, instead of taking it away.

q.cb.none.text: Undo the last step first, then the first step. That is how every two-step equation comes apart.

p.intro.text: Sam solves two x plus eight equals twenty like this. Divide by two to get x plus eight equals ten, so x equals two. Is Sam right?

p.test.text: Let's test it. Build the argument, and see where it leads.

p.build.text: Now prove it. Fill each because with the reason that makes the line true.

p.no.move.text: Moving is a shortcut name, not a reason. The reason is that eight comes off both pans, so they stay level.

p.no.some.text: That is exactly Sam's slip. Dividing a side by two means dividing every term on it.

p.no.other.text: True, but it is the reason for a different line. Which reason makes this line true?

p.c1.text: Right. Sam halved the bags and the right pan, but not the eight loose marbles, so the balance tips.

p.c2.text: Right. Eight off both pans keeps them level: two x equals twelve.

p.c3.text: Right. Split both pans into two equal shares: one bag balances six. And two times six, plus eight, is twenty.

p.done.text: That's a proof: three claims, each with its reason, and the balance backs every one. Sam divided only some of the terms.
